name: Meksiko
description: Meksiko is the most popular trick-taking game in Serbia, played by three players with a 32-card deck. It is an Auction Whist variant where players bid on the number of tricks they will take, with the highest bid 'Meksiko' being an undertaking to win all tricks without the talon and with no trumps. The game combines bidding strategy with precise trick-taking play.

overview.description: Meksiko is the most popular trick-taking game in Serbia, played by three players with a 32-card deck. It is an Auction Whist variant where players bid on the number of tricks they will take, with the highest bid 'Meksiko' being an undertaking to win all tricks without the talon and with no trumps. The game combines bidding strategy with precise trick-taking play.

history.origins: Meksiko was likely inspired by Preference, a similar game popular in Eastern Europe. The game has no actual connection to Mexico - 'Meksiko' is simply the Serbian spelling used as the name of the highest bid.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Likely developed from Preference variants
Mid-20th Century: Becomes the most popular trick-taking game in Serbia
Present: Widely played throughout Serbia and Serbian communities abroad
history.cultural: A staple of Serbian social life, played in homes, cafes, and clubs. The game is considered a test of skill and character.
history.evolution: The game's unique bidding structure, particularly the 'Meksiko' bid, distinguishes it from its Preference ancestor.

setup.players: 3 players (standard). Can be played with 4 if the dealer sits out each hand.
setup.deck: 32-card pack (7 through Ace in each suit). Ranking: A (high), K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 (low). Often played with Hungarian cards (William Tell pattern).
setup.dealing: 10 cards to each player, dealt in packets. The remaining 2 cards form the talon (kup).

rules.objective: Win the number of tricks bid, or prevent the declarer from making their bid. First to 51 points wins the game.
rules.gameplay: The declarer leads to the first trick. Players must follow suit if possible. If unable to follow, may play any card. Highest trump wins, or highest card of led suit if no trumps.
keyRules: Meksiko bid: win all 10 tricks, no talon, no trumps
Declarer takes talon (except in Meksiko) and chooses trumps
Discarded talon cards count as won tricks for declarer

strategy.basic: Only bid what you think you can make. Count your high cards and consider the talon's potential. In defense, try to force the declarer to use trumps early.
strategy.intermediate: The talon exchange is crucial - discard cards that don't help your contract. Watch opponents' play to deduce their holdings. Coordinate with the other defender to stop the declarer.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is essential. Track all trumps and high cards. Bluff in bidding to push opponents into difficult contracts. The Meksiko bid requires perfect hand evaluation.
tips: Don't overbid - failing a contract gives opponents significant points
Save your highest trumps for critical tricks
If defending, try to make the declarer guess which defender has which cards
The Meksiko bid should only be attempted with an exceptional hand

scoring.description: Points are awarded based on the bid and whether it was made. Target is 51 points.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach 51 points wins the game.
